correctness.rationale: The ordinary graph discrete-Morse complex uses oriented incidence pairs v->w as vertices, not graph-edge matchings. Its exact six-vertex triangular-prism incidence enumeration produces face-vector (18,126,428,705,450) with 1727 nonempty simplices. In a fully separate implementation each vertex selected at most one incident outgoing arrow, each undirected graph edge at most once, and all directed cycles were excluded. Independent F2 boundary ranks (17,109,319,386) plus top-dimensional rational rank bounds establish H4(X;Q)=Q^64 with other positive rational homology zero; integral H4 is a free kernel of rank64. On the layer-interchange τ, signed fixed-face traces are (0,-6,0,+9,0), giving Lefschetz -3 and top trace -4, hence rational eigen-dimensions p=30 and q=34. Independent top 450-column mod-two kernel enumeration gives 64 binary generators and rank(τ-I) on this kernel equal to 30. The integral involution-lattice theorem decomposes every free Z[C2]-lattice as regular^r plus positive^(p-r) plus negative^(q-r), because L/(L^+⊕L^-) injects into both mod2 eigenspace lattices and consists of diagonal half-integral gluing. Therefore H4(X;Z)=Z[C2]^30 ⊕ Z_-^4 exactly. This finite lattice classification does not follow from the known rational trace alone.
